question: In the context of British rule in India, who among the following Governor-Generals created a professional cadre of company servants making provisions for them for generous salaries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Cornwallis**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** was the Governor-General of India from 1786 to 1793.
 
• He is known for creating a professional cadre of company servants and making provisions for them for generous salaries.
 
• His reforms, known as the **Cornwallis Code**, included measures to curb corruption among company officials by paying them adequately.
 
• Lord Cornwallis also introduced significant judicial and administrative reforms in British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Warren Hastings**, who served before Cornwallis, laid the foundation for British administration in India but did not implement such a professional cadre.
 
• **Lord Mayo** and **Lord Dalhousie** also served as Governor-Generals but were known for other reforms and administrative measures.
 
• The Cornwallis Code also included the introduction of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, which restructured land revenue collection.
 
• His tenure marked the beginning of a more systematic and bureaucratic approach to governance in British India.
